title: gradle-wrapper.json — the wrapper fetch-path verification document
description: Emitted by bin/gradle-wrapper-verify.mjs into CW_REPORT_DIR. Declared because its sibling scannerFindings rows were schema-validated while this document was not, so a consumer could not tell a renamed field from one that was never there. additionalProperties is false ON PURPOSE: a new key must be declared here before it can ship, which is the only thing that makes the absence of a key mean anything.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601. Honours CW_NOW so runs are byte-reproducible.

root.description: Repo root, HOME collapsed to ~ so the document does not leak a local path.

ran.description: Always true in a written document — a run that did not happen writes nothing at all. Present so a consumer reading a merged corpus can tell an absent document from a present one.

applicable.description: false means the repo ships no Gradle wrapper. NOT a pass: nothing was verified. Consumers must not fold it into a clean count.

reason.description: Why applicable is false. Present only in that case.

findings.description: Always an array, including when applicable is false — an absent array and an empty one are the same claim and only one of them throws in a consumer doing .findings.length.

scope.description: What was verified. Travels WITH the counts so a reader cannot take the finding total for a verdict on the whole build.

doesNotCover.description: The named blind spots. Required to be non-empty when present: a scope disclosure that lists nothing asserts total coverage by omission.

declaredVersion.description: null means the properties file was read and carried no parseable version — distinct from the key being absent, which means it was never read.

jarMatchesVersion.description: The Gradle version the known-good list attributes this jar hash to. May differ from declaredVersion; that difference is the signal.

checksumCheck.description: 'no-reference-list' and 'unreadable' are UNKNOWNS, not passes — monitor/unknown.mjs maps both. Only 'known' is a verified match.
